Even the merchant will scarce find reason to repent his having been introduced to the acquaintance of Plato and Cicero. But still, if the circumstances of the parent, or any other just reason, should render it inconvenient to send the young man who is intended for trade to a free school to study the ancient languages, means may be easily adopted to make up for his loss. Though you burden him not with Latin and Greek, yet strive to inspire him with a taste for useful knowledge and for elegant literature.
